UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user of the HR Augmentation System, linked to an external authentication system. This entity stores application-specific user data rather than authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. This ID is intended to correspond to the user's identifier from the external authentication provider (e.g., Google's user ID).

email.description: The primary email address of the user, used for display and internal application purposes. This is assumed to be provided by the external authentication system.

displayName.description: The user's preferred display name, typically fetched from the external authentication system.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was first created in the HRAi Dashboard system.

lastLogin.description: Timestamp of the user's most recent login to the HRAi Dashboard application.

JobPost.title: JobPost
JobPost.description: Represents a structured job post generated by the AI based on a user-provided job description.

id.description: Unique identifier for the JobPost entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who initiated the generation of this job post. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N JobPost)

originalDescription.description: The raw, unstructured job description text input by the user.

generatedTitle.description: The title of the structured job post generated by the AI.

generatedContent.description: The complete, structured job post content generated by the LLM tool.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the job post was originally generated.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the job post was last modified, if applicable.

Candidate.title: Candidate
Candidate.description: Represents a job candidate whose information is managed within the system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Candidate entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who is managing this candidate's application. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Candidate)

fullName.description: The full name of the candidate.

email.description: The primary email address of the candidate.

resumeScore.description: A numerical score assigned to the candidate's resume, typically by an AI, indicating its relevance or quality.

status.description: The current stage of the candidate in the recruitment process (e.g., 'Shortlisted', 'Interviewing', 'Offer Extended', 'Hired', 'Rejected').

applicationDate.description: The date when the candidate's application was received or entered into the system.

notes.description: General notes or comments pertaining to the candidate's application or profile.

Interview.title: Interview
Interview.description: Records the details and AI-generated results of an interview conducted with a candidate.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Interview entity.

candidateId.description: Reference to the Candidate who participated in this interview. (Relationship: Candidate 1:N Interview)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who is managing or initiated this interview process. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Interview)

interviewDate.description: The date and time when the interview was conducted.

status.description: The current status of the interview (e.g., 'Completed', 'Scheduled', 'Processing Feedback', 'Canceled').

performanceScore.description: A numerical score reflecting the candidate's overall performance during the interview, typically assessed by AI.

feedbackSummary.description: A concise summary of the AI's feedback and observations from the interview.

detailedFeedback.description: More extensive or raw feedback details generated by the AI from the interview session.

interviewType.description: The specific type or focus of the interview (e.g., 'AI Screening', 'Technical Assessment', 'Behavioral Interview').

Contract.title: Contract
Contract.description: Represents a dynamically generated contract or offer letter for a candidate.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Contract entity.

candidateId.description: Reference to the Candidate for whom this contract is generated. (Relationship: Candidate 1:N Contract)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who generated or is managing this contract. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Contract)

title.description: The title or subject of the contract (e.g., 'Employment Offer Letter', 'Consulting Agreement').

generatedContent.description: The full text content of the dynamically generated contract document.

status.description: The current status of the contract in its lifecycle (e.g., 'Draft', 'Sent for Signature', 'Signed', 'Rejected').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the contract was first generated.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the contract was last updated or modified.

effectiveDate.description: The date when the terms of the contract are or were to become effective.

TimesheetEntry.title: TimesheetEntry
TimesheetEntry.description: Represents a single task or event entry in a user's timesheet, which can be synced from external calendars or manually added.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TimesheetEntry entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile to whom this timesheet entry belongs. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N TimesheetEntry)

eventDate.description: The date and time when the event or task associated with this timesheet entry occurred.

taskDescription.description: A descriptive summary of the task or event.

durationMinutes.description: The duration of the task or event in minutes.

sourceEventId.description: The original identifier of the event from the external source (e.g., Google Calendar event ID), if applicable.

sourceType.description: The source from which this timesheet entry originated (e.g., 'Google Calendar', 'Manual Entry', 'Gmail').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this timesheet entry was recorded in the system.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Stores notifications and alerts received from external sources (e.g., email, Telegram) or generated by the system for a specific user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Notification entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile to whom this notification is directed. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Notification)

message.description: The full content or body of the notification message.

type.description: The category or source of the notification (e.g., 'Email', 'Telegram', 'System Alert', 'Reminder').

timestamp.description: The date and time when the notification was received or generated.

isRead.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the user has viewed or marked this notification as read.

link.description: An optional URL or deep link associated with the notification, providing more details or direct navigation.

definition.description: Stores the profile information for a specific user. The document ID for a UserProfile is its unique 'userId', corresponding to the authenticated user's ID. This path enforces owner-based access, where a user can only read/write their own profile.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching 'request.auth.uid'.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed around user-centric, private data, adhering strictly to the core design principles of Authorization Independence and QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters). All user-specific data is strictly segregated under a dedicated user path, ensuring maximum security and simplifying rule logic.

1.  **Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** Every document in a subcollection (e.g., JobPost, Candidate, Interview, Contract, TimesheetEntry, Notification) explicitly includes the `userId` field. For Interview and Contract entities, the `candidateId` is also denormalized within the document. This critical denormalization strategy eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules, which would otherwise introduce complex, non-atomic authorization dependencies. By having `request.auth.uid` match the `{userId}` in the path and the `userId` field within the document, authorization checks become atomic and highly performant.

2.  **Structural Segregation & QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters):** All user-owned data is stored under `/users/{userId}/...`. This structural segregation ensures that all documents within a given subcollection (e.g., `/users/{userId}/jobPosts`) belong to the `{userId}` specified in the path. This pattern directly supports QAPs because `list` operations automatically inherit the `userId` from the path. A user can only list documents from their own `/users/{uid}/` path, making it impossible to accidentally (or maliciously) fetch data belonging to other users. Security rules can simply verify that `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path) and `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` (from the document), providing robust, debuggable, and performant authorization.

3.  **Hierarchical Ownership:** For entities like `Interview` and `Contract` which are strongly associated with a `Candidate`, the path continues to nest them under `candidates`. For example, `/users/{userId}/candidates/{candidateId}/interviews/{interviewId}`. This not only provides logical organization but also enables precise scoping for queries and rules (e.g., listing all interviews for a specific candidate managed by the authenticated user). The denormalized `userId` and `candidateId` within the `Interview` and `Contract` documents maintain authorization independence even at this deeper level of nesting.

4.  **Predictability and Consistency:** Standardized field names like `userId` and descriptive wildcards (e.g., `{jobPostId}`, `{candidateId}`) contribute to a predictable and easily auditable structure. The document ID for `UserProfile` is designed to be the `userId` from Firebase Auth (`request.auth.uid`), directly linking the authentication system to the application data.
